stimulus: Grant officer: The Halloway Fund supports projects that are likely to expand public access to the performing arts. The Delta Theater's application proposes free weekend matinees in neighborhoods that have no permanent performance venue, and its budget is, by the Fund's usual standards, a modest one. So the Delta Theater's project is one the Halloway Fund is likely to support.
question_stem: The grant officer's argument depends on assuming which one of the following?
choice_a: The Halloway Fund supports every project that would expand public access to the performing arts while staying within a modest budget.
choice_b: The Delta Theater has successfully staged free public performances in previous seasons.
choice_c: If the Halloway Fund is likely to support a project, that project will expand public access to the performing arts.
choice_d: It was the absence of performance venues in those neighborhoods that led the Delta Theater to propose weekend matinees there.
choice_e: Free weekend matinees in neighborhoods without a permanent performance venue would be likely to expand public access to the performing arts.
prediction_text: The premises describe the proposal; the Fund's criterion is expanding access. Predict the bridge: this proposal meets that criterion.
trap_a: too strong - a sufficient-style universal the argument never needs (survivor)
trap_b: helpful background that fails the negation test (survivor)
trap_c: reverses the conditional direction of the bridge
trap_d: causal origin story the argument does not need
explanation_a: The argument concludes only that support is likely; it does not require that the Fund back every qualifying project. Deny this and the argument can still stand.
explanation_b: A strong track record would help, but the argument survives its denial - it rests on what the proposal is, not on past seasons.
explanation_c: This runs from support to access; the argument needs the opposite bridge, from this proposal's features to likely access expansion.
explanation_d: Why the theater chose those neighborhoods is immaterial; the argument needs the matinees to expand access, whatever prompted them.
explanation_e: Correct. Deny it - suppose such matinees would not expand access - and the premises no longer connect to the Fund's criterion; the conclusion collapses. The argument must assume it.
